sentences.text: Portugal held three general elections in just over three years. Who keeps calling them?
Who can vote? Portuguese citizens from 18, even abroad, plus Brazilians living here with equal rights.
The ballot has no names, only parties. You put one cross next to the party you choose.
Each of the 22 districts shares its seats by vote share. Lisbon 48, Portalegre just two.
The 230 members of the Assembly make the laws and can bring down the government. There is no second chamber.
In 2025, Prime Minister Montenegro's alliance won 91 seats, far short of a majority.
But he didn't need a majority. The President appointed him, and he governs until a majority votes him out.
And the President? Directly elected, he can veto laws and dissolve parliament. That's how Portugal got its last three elections.
Should one person be able to send a whole country back to the polls?
